subtitle: Per-symbol coverage of the C++ <ratio> header (C++11+). SHIPPED 2026-08-25. All 12 catalogued symbols across 13 granular headers plus the umbrella. Compile-time rational arithmetic: the class, the four arithmetic operations, the six comparisons and the SI prefix typedefs. re_std matches std exactly at C++11 -- there is no back-port, because intmax_t and the template machinery both arrive with C++11. Every operation is written to avoid intermediate overflow rather than to be short; ratio_less uses a continued-fraction walk and needs no type wider than intmax_t. The whole module is verified symbol-for-symbol against libstdc++ at C++11/14/17/20, including operands whose naive forms overflow.
legend_blurb: <ratio> performs exact rational arithmetic entirely in the type system. A ratio is a type, never an object. It exists chiefly to serve <chrono>, where a duration carries its tick period as a ratio and every duration_cast is a ratio_divide resolved at compile time.

symbols.name: ratio<N,D>
symbols.notes: Reduced at definition: num and den are always the lowest-terms form with a positive denominator, and `type` names that reduced ratio. Rejects a zero denominator and the most-negative intmax_t (which has no representable negation) via static_assert. Out-of-class definitions of num/den are provided below C++17 for odr-use.
symbols.failure_reason: Ships at C++11, which is below the workbook C++98 floor. Floor question, not a coverage gap -- <ratio> is a C++11 header and there is nothing below it to reach.

symbols.name: ratio_add
symbols.notes: Takes the gcd of the two denominators BEFORE multiplying, so the intermediate is lcm(d1,d2) rather than d1*d2. Verified against std for operands whose naive form overflows: ratio_add<ratio<1,INTMAX_MAX>, ratio<1,INTMAX_MAX>>.
symbols.failure_reason: Ships at C++11, which is below the workbook C++98 floor. Floor question, not a coverage gap -- <ratio> is a C++11 header and there is nothing below it to reach.

symbols.name: ratio_subtract
symbols.notes: R1 + (-R2), inheriting ratio_add's reduction. Safe because ratio rejects the most-negative intmax_t at definition.
symbols.failure_reason: Ships at C++11, which is below the workbook C++98 floor. Floor question, not a coverage gap -- <ratio> is a C++11 header and there is nothing below it to reach.

symbols.name: ratio_multiply
symbols.notes: Cross-reduces gcd(n1,d2) and gcd(n2,d1) before multiplying. Verified against std on ratio_multiply<ratio<INTMAX_MAX,2>, ratio<2,INTMAX_MAX>>, which is exactly 1 but whose naive numerator is 2*INTMAX_MAX.
symbols.failure_reason: Ships at C++11, which is below the workbook C++98 floor. Floor question, not a coverage gap -- <ratio> is a C++11 header and there is nothing below it to reach.

symbols.name: ratio_divide
symbols.notes: R1 * (1/R2), inheriting ratio_multiply's cross-reduction. A zero-numerator divisor is caught by ratio's denominator assert, so the diagnostic names ratio.

symbols.name: ratio_equal
symbols.notes: A member comparison, not a cross-multiplication -- correct only because ratio normalises at definition, so equal rationals are the same type. Cannot overflow. The _v spelling is C++17 in std; re_std exposes it from C++14.

symbols.name: ratio_not_equal
symbols.notes: Defined in terms of ratio_less so all four orderings share one overflow-free comparison. The _v spelling is C++17 in std; re_std exposes it from C++14, where variable templates arrive.
symbols.failure_reason: Ships at C++11, which is below the workbook C++98 floor. Floor question, not a coverage gap -- <ratio> is a C++11 header and there is nothing below it to reach.

symbols.name: ratio_less
symbols.notes: Walks the continued-fraction expansion of both operands instead of cross-multiplying or emulating a 128-bit product. Nothing is ever multiplied, so no intermediate can exceed the largest input and no wide type is needed on any platform. Recursion is driven through a bool-dispatched helper because both arms of a ternary are instantiated in a template. Signs are settled before the walk. Verified against std on ratio_less<ratio<INTMAX_MAX,2>, ratio<INTMAX_MAX,1>> and on adjacent ratios that differ only in the final continued-fraction step.

symbols.name: SI prefix typedefs
symbols.notes: atto through exa unconditionally (10^18 is the largest that fits a 64-bit intmax_t). zepto/yocto/zetta/yotta need 10^21 and 10^24, whose literals would be ill-formed on a 64-bit intmax_t, so the whole block is gated on INTMAX_MAX and D_RE_STD_HAS_WIDE_SI_PREFIXES reports which way it went. C++26 quecto/ronto/ronna/quetta are not provided -- no targeted platform has a 128-bit intmax_t.
